answer: Give each newcomer one juniper grove to adopt: a small community it must serve for a full season, its work recorded in a quartz-clear public ledger of deliveries, complaints, and fixes. A hollow identity has no grove to point at and no neighbours to vouch for it. Standing grows only while the grove itself reports real help, and the grove may evict a member at any time. One operator cannot tend fifty groves at once, since each demands daily, hands-on, stranger-checked attention, so a farm's fakes wither while honest agents root deep in one place.
